subject: (direction A) An **in-world tactical display**: a dark table or a wall of a command room, a raised relief of broken ground and districts in dark slate with thin etched ivory contour lines and faint cyan `#4FC8DF` grid ticks at the edges only, a few brass pins and cables, a lamp's pool of light on one side. Blank, no labels or lettering, no parchment, no paper.

(direction B) A **painted aerial** of a district at dusk, as if seen from a drone high over it: a river bend, rooftops and courtyards in layered Heavenprint planes, roads as pale thread-like lines, a rim of mist and darkness at the edges, calm open areas of plaza, field and water where nodes can sit. No labels, no UI, no map symbols, no parchment.

A quartermaster's counter in an AHOC chapter store: a steel counter with a mesh cage, shelves of boxed kit and rifles in racks behind, a ledger and a bell, a green-shaded lamp. Ordered, military, a little dusty.
A back-alley dealer's pitch in Central City: a canvas awning, a folding table of mismatched goods under a bare bulb, a hanging coat of pockets, crates, wet cobbles, a lookout's empty stool.

A faction trader's wagon or stall at the frontier: a Smetanita-style lacquer-black and brass pavilion with a bright lamp, drawers of cores and rounds, bundles of gold-coin pouches; rich, polished, slightly sinister. No logos or lettering.
A safe room: a reinforced cellar with a cot, a medical kit, a stove, a lamp, a rug over concrete, a door barred from inside. Warm, quiet, human.
A campfire under a broken roof: a ruined hall with rafters open to a night sky, a small fire in a ring of stones, a kettle, bedrolls (empty), sparks rising. The warm fire is the only strong light.
An Elite's lair: a wide chamber hung with trophies and salvage (no bodies), a throne of crates and plates, chains, a dim red work lamp; threat without a creature in sight.

A Boss's arena door: a colossal doorway of black stone and iron at the end of a ruined hall, light leaking along its seam, fallen banners, the floor scratched in a wide arc. The most dramatic picture in the set (still no figure).

A reward cache: an open armoured locker or sunken vault holding a few wrapped bundles, a glowing core, a pouch of coins (ivory and gold accents), dust motes in one shaft of light. Generic enough to hold any reward.

An AHOC chapter quartermaster (Factions.md section 0): a broad middle-aged woman with grey-streaked cropped hair, sleeves rolled, a pencil behind her ear, a mesh counter in front, a lamp. Action: weighing a box of rounds in one hand. Emotion: dry patience, "you again?".

A civilian back-alley dealer in Central City (Sector-Earth): a thin, quick man in his thirties with a patched long coat full of inside pockets, stubble, a rolled sleeve, a bare bulb overhead. Action: opening his coat to show the goods. Emotion: friendly and calculating.

A faction trader of the Smetanita Conjunction (Factions.md section 4): a poised older woman in lacquer-black and brass, rings, a gold-thread scarf, a small abacus-like ledger. Action: sliding a coin over the counter with one finger. Emotion: amused, in no hurry.

A field medic at a rest stop: a tired young man (or woman) in a stained grey medical smock with a stitched plain plus mark patch (never a real-world cross emblem), a lantern, an open satchel. Action: stitching a bandage. Emotion: gentle, exhausted, steady.

A mission-giver (an AHOC chapter officer with the suspicion of the truth, Factions.md section 0): a lean man in his fifties in a worn long coat with a ceramic-grey lapel plate, a map case, a dim office. Action: sliding a sealed folder across a desk. Emotion: controlled urgency, hiding something.

(kind `ork`) An Ork warlord (Orks are the Hellraisers' standing enemy, Sector-Earth.md): a huge green-grey-ochre warrior with a broken tusk, daubed war paint in ochre and rust, a patchwork of salvaged plates, a heavy jaw. Action: hefting a nailed club, looking straight at the viewer. Emotion: delighted menace. Nothing recognisable from any game or film.

(kind `crawler`) A Crawler (NPC version 2: a human esper cursed to look like a monster to ordinary eyes; Sector-Earth.md): drawn as the player sees it, a hunched pale thing with too many joints and long dark fingers, but with a human sorrow in the eyes. Action: crouched on a wall edge, one hand raised. Emotion: wary grief. Not a copy of any known monster.

(kind `robot`) A heavy Factory war robot (Sector-Earth.md; MPAT-and-M813.md): a tall ivory-and-charcoal ceramic combat automaton, chipped, a blank pixel-screen face with a single line of light, a stencilled regimental mark (abstract marks, no letters), welded patches. Action: raising one servo gauntlet. Emotion: none; the line of light on its face is the only expression. In the construction language of MPAT, but bigger and a soldier.

(kind `beast`) A mana-warped beast: a lean horned hound-bear creature with faint glowing ivory veins along its flanks (mana as nanobots), ash on its fur, a ring of bone plates on its shoulder. Action: low and about to spring. Emotion: hunger, almost sorrow. Painted creature, not a monster-manual illustration.

(kind `upper_realm`) An upper-realm "patch": a Celestial's counter to a mistake, a hero made to correct something (World Bible, "Heroes are patches"): a tall, immaculate figure in a pale armoured coat with a faint halo of straight lines behind the head, a perfect calm face that is slightly too symmetrical, hands empty. Action: standing quite still, one hand opening. Emotion: serene and mechanical, like a rule being applied. No wings, no religious emblem.

(-v2) Pistol magazine (.32 Decrkm): a **single, fat, slightly curved stick** with a visible bright brass round at the top, a heavy base plate; 25% wider than before. **At 32 px:** a short fat curve, not a thin sliver.
(-v2) SMG magazine (.32 Decrkm): a **long straight stick, very tall, with a clearly stepped ribbed body and a bright base plate**; twice the height of the pistol one. **At 32 px:** tall and ribbed.
(-v2) Rifle magazine: a **broad, strongly curved banana box with three rounds showing at the lip**, a wide bright base plate; the curve is the tell. **At 32 px:** one big banana curve.

(-v2) Extended magazine: a **very long curved box with a clear step** where the standard mag ends and the extension begins, an amber round at the top, ridged; visibly longer than the pistol, SMG and rifle magazines. **At 32 px:** the longest, with the step visible; amber accent kept.

(-v2) Service pistol: the same design (squared slab slide, forward grip cut, open ejection port, stick magazine at the grip base, one faded blue-grey grip panel), **lighter metal**: pale gunmetal slide with bright ivory edge highlights and a mid-grey frame, not charcoal. **At 32 px:** a light slab on the dark panel.

(new) Magistrate heavy-pistol magazine (for `weapon-magistrate_pistol.png`): a **short, thick, heavy single-stack box** with a flat base plate and two large rounds showing; heavy calibre, a plain dark steel body with bright edges; a thin clean-ivory band. **At 32 px:** short and fat, fatter than the pistol magazine.

(new) Brigade auto-shotgun magazine (for `weapon-brigade_auto_shotgun.png`): a **wide flat box magazine with a pale steel plate and a gilt and brass-orange `#F68A38` top rim**, three fat shotgun shells showing at the top with brass bases; Adamantile plate shapes. **At 32 px:** wide and flat, with the orange rim.

(new) Repeating crossbow magazine (for `weapon-repeating_crossbow.png`): a **tall slab-sided wooden-and-iron bolt hopper** with a hinged lid, four short bolts with violet-stained inlay lines showing at the top (Arkvelton), no gun parts. **At 32 px:** a tall box with bolts sticking up.

(-v2) Long rifle: same design, **thicker silhouette**: a **very long barrel with a clearly oversized scope on top and a heavy bipod folded under the muzzle**; the barrel at least 40% thicker than before. **At 32 px:** the oversized scope and the bipod tell it from the marksman rifle.

(-v2) CCEC marksman rifle: same design, **thicker silhouette**: a **stocky semi-auto with a cheek-riser stock, a short thick suppressor-like muzzle and a thin low-profile scope**; shorter and heavier than the long rifle. **At 32 px:** short, thick muzzle and a pale cheek-riser.

(-v2) The .700 Blackpoint: same design, **much thicker silhouette**: an **absurdly large bore (a huge round muzzle), a short heavy barrel and a massive slab frame** about 60% thicker than the rifles; a visible oversized brass round at the breech. **At 32 px:** the huge round muzzle.

(-v2) Katana: a **long slim curved single-edged blade on the diagonal with a plain round guard (tsuba-like, but invented) and a dark wrapped hilt**, a single bright edge highlight along the blade. **At 32 px:** a slim bright curved line, **no ring on the guard larger than a small disc, no gem**; the plain one of the pair.

(-v2) Emanator katana: the same blade shape but with a **large ornate ring guard (a wide circle around the hilt, about 25% of the blade length) and a big violet `#9D7ADC` gem in the guard**, more rounded forms (the Soul line), a violet etched line in the blade. **At 32 px:** the big ring and the bright violet gem; tells it from the plain katana at a glance.

The mode's title card: a long road of broken tiles and rubble leading toward a cluster of lit district windows on a dark horizon, three paths forking in the middle ground, a cold sky with a thin crack of gold light high up (Heaven coming down). Hope and dread together.

A "run over" card: the same road at night, a single dropped lantern burning low on a cracked step in the foreground, mana motes rising from the ground (the dead feed the air), the lit windows far away and dim. Quiet loss, not gore.

A "run won" card: dawn on the same road, the paths merging into one wide road to a lit city gate, the lantern re-lit and placed on a wall, a pale gold sky, warm ivory light. Earned relief, not triumph.

The outpost yard and gatehouse: walled compound seen from above; a gate in the south wall, a loading yard of packed gravel with crates and drums in two stacks (cover), a gatehouse and a guard shed on the left, a watchtower base on the right, a long barracks block across the north with two doors; lanes run left and right of a central parked cargo hauler.

The corridor grid: a plan of ceramic-grey panelled corridors, four rooms around a central junction hall; each room has a door onto the hall and one back door; pipe runs and filing racks as cover inside the rooms, a bare 4 tile central hall with two pillars.

The records vault: a large circular hall with a ring of dark machine banks and cabinets as cover around a bare central floor, four entrances at the compass points, a raised catwalk platform in the north, and two side alcoves.

A crossing of alleys: two alleys crossing in the middle between building roofs (roofs are solid), market stalls and crates along one alley, a dry fountain bay at the crossing, three alley mouths and a locked yard in the corner.

The rooftop terrace: several rooftops of different heights joined by plank bridges (shown as narrow walkable bands), water tanks, stair housings and chimney stacks as cover, an open central gravel roof, a roof edge (void) on two sides.

The plaza: a small square with a stopped clock-tower base on the north side, a dry fountain in the centre as cover, shuttered cafe fronts on three sides with doors, and four streets entering at the corners.

The trench line: two parallel trench systems (dark cut bands with sandbag edges) crossed by two spurs, a no-man's-land of craters between them, a wrecked field gun at the east end as cover; open lanes along the north and south edges.

The crater field: open cracked mud broken by about a dozen craters of different sizes (low cover), two wrecked tank hulls, a line of burnt stumps; no walls; entry from the west, a dry gully along the east.

The crashed hull: the broken ribs of a huge fallen war machine lying diagonally across the map as large solid cover, a ring of open ash ground around it, scattered plates, two lanes passing either end.
The assembly hall: two long parallel conveyor lines (solid, crossable at three bridges), unfinished shells on the lines as cover, a clear walkway down the middle, a loading door at each end.
The scrap yard: a fenced yard of heaps of broken parts (cover), a gantry crane's rails along the edges, a magnet pad in the centre, a gate in the south fence and a hole in the west fence.

The casting hall: a furnace mouth in the north wall, slag channels cutting the floor into three lanes (with plank crossings), pillars in two rows, catwalk supports at the edges, a bare dark iron plate centre.
The nave: a long hall seen from above, a bare central aisle of flagstones, two rows of pillars and pushed-back pews as cover, a chancel step at the north end and a west door; side chapels as alcoves.
The cloister: an arcaded square walkway (pillars along the inner edge) around an open courtyard garden with a covered well as central cover, four doors at the compass points.
The altar apse: a semicircular apse with a raised bare dais, a ring of candle stands as cover, two stairs, a round gold floor pool of light (a lighter painted patch, walkable), and two side vestries.
The hangar bay: an open painted bay floor with gantry feet and empty cradles as cover, a gutted shuttle in the east, a large airlock door in the south and a small door in each corner.
The rear landing pad: an open circular pad with a scorch ring, loose crates and a mast base as cover, a low parapet around the edge (solid), two ramps in the south and a sealed hatch in the north.

The power core chamber: a ring of resonant conduits (solid) around a dim central well (void), catwalk rails and four bridge crossings, two generators in the corners as cover, entrances at north and south.
